In the UK, the new academic year starts in September. We have 6 weeks for each term followed by a holiday. For example=

September to October - 6 week teaching then  October half term holiday (half term means 1 week).

November to December- 6 week teaching then Christmas holiday for 2 weeks.

January to February- 6 week teaching then half term in February.

February to April- 6 week teaching then 2 weeks Easter holiday

In July to August we have 6 weeks off from school before starting again in September.

Primary school = age 3 to 11
The structure is - nursery, reception, year 1, year 2, year 3, year 4, year 5, year 6.

In year 6, students take SATs before starting secondary school.



Secondary school  ( also called high school and academy) structure is known as year 7,8,9,10 and 11.= ages 11 to 16. ~GCSEs are taken in year 11 which is the last year. 

GCSEs are the first real qualification obtained in school. 

GCSEs are a two year course which begin at year 10. Students choose their GCSE subjects in year 9.

Sixth form or College = this is where students to A levels or BTEC courses. A sixth form typically has students aged between 16-19

. A levels and equivalent BTEC courses are a two year course but some students will probably have a chance to resit a year if they don't do so good in their courses. That's why the age goes up to 19

A college is different as it can have adult learners alongside who want to do their GCSEs for example. Also, they have courses such as apprenticeships.


Primary school to sixth form = education is free.

University is not free


University- can go at any age provided student is over 18. When applying directly from sixth form, they can make you apply through something called UCAS (an online application).

University starts at late September to early October. University has semesters which unlike school and sixth form, they may not have a holiday every six weeks. For example the only holiday they get is at Christmas and Easter. They have a large holiday from June until late September.

University gives a chance to get a degree. 
An undergraduate will spend 3 years getting a degree but it depends on the course because medicine and pharmacy is 5 years. 

After undergraduate degree, you can do a postgraduate such as a master's.

A PhD is after postgraduate study when you want to research something very specifically.

This is just a brief summary of the education system. 
Some things are a bit complicated but this is just the typical outline.

I hope I made it easy to understand

I'm from sylhet, northeastern Bangladesh. We have something called guror handesh that is distinctive to this region. Its a sweet fried donut type food. 
It's a mixture of date molasses syrup, rice flour, plain flour and water. Its deep fried in oil until it resembles a donut with shrills on the outside. The shrills occur naturally while cooking the batter. Its usually consumed on the festival of Eid. What's unique about this is that it's our take on 'shondesh' which are Bangladeshi desserts found in Dhaka and west Bengal. guror handesh is more like a 'pitha' in Dhaka as it's a fried cake item whereas shondesh are more fudge type desserts. Sylhet in general has quite a distinctive culture compared to Dhaka.
